a2-01.explain: The preterite tells what happened: finished actions, one after another. He/she form: -ar verbs add -ó (llegar > llegó, mirar > miró); -er/-ir verbs add -ió (correr > corrió, subir > subió). They form: -aron / -ieron (llegaron, corrieron). I and you (tú) forms: -é / -aste (llegué, llegaste) and -í / -iste (perdí, perdiste). Watch out: the accent changes the meaning. Llegó = she arrived; llego = I arrive.
examples: Ana llegó tarde a la estación de Madrid.
Ana arrived late at the Madrid station.
Luego miró el andén número cuatro.
Then she looked at platform number four.
Los dos corrieron a la calle y subieron al autobús.
The two of them ran to the street and got on the bus.

a2-01.explain: Some very common verbs are irregular in the preterite. Ver > vio: like other one-syllable forms (dio, fue), it has no written accent. Decir changes its stem to dij- and ends in -o, not -ió: dijo; they: dijeron (not 'dijieron'). Learn these as whole words. Watch out: 'vió' and 'dició' are typical learner mistakes.
examples: Ana miró su teléfono y vio un mensaje de su madre.
Ana looked at her phone and saw a message from her mother.
—Perdí el tren de las nueve —dijo Ana—.
"I missed the nine o'clock train," said Ana.
—¡Qué suerte! —dijo Ana—.
"What luck!" said Ana.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.explain: Ir a + infinitive talks about the near future: voy a llegar = I'm going to arrive. Ir a + place is simple movement: voy a Valencia = I'm going to Valencia. Check what follows the a: a verb means a plan, a place means a destination. Watch out: never drop the a ('voy llegar' is wrong), and a + el = al: vamos al pueblo.
examples: Perdí el tren, pero voy a llegar primero.
I missed the train, but I'm going to arrive first.
Me llamo Pablo y también voy a Valencia.
My name is Pablo and I'm going to Valencia too.
Hoy voy a tocar la guitarra en la boda.
Today I'm going to play the guitar at the wedding.

a2-02.explain: To tell a friend to do something (positive tú command), use the he/she present form: busca (buscar), lleva (llevar), camina (caminar). A few common verbs have short irregular commands: ir > ve, venir > ven, hacer > haz, poner > pon, salir > sal, decir > di, tener > ten. Watch out: 'go!' is ve, not vas or va.
examples: Primero, ve al mercado y busca a doña Fabiola
First, go to the market and look for Doña Fabiola.
Luego, lleva los mangos a la panadería de la plaza
Then take the mangoes to the bakery on the square.
¡Ve!
Go!

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.explain: Indirect pronouns say to/for whom: me, te, le (to him/her/you), nos, les. They go before a conjugated verb: le dio = gave (to) her. With two pronouns, the indirect one comes first, then the direct one: te lo regala = gives it to you (lo = the puppy, el cachorro). Watch out: 'gave her a bag' is le dio, not la dio, because she receives the bag.
examples: Doña Fabiola le dio una bolsa de mangos y otro papel.
Doña Fabiola gave her a bag of mangoes and another note.
Ella te lo regala.
She's giving him to you (as a gift).
En la panadería, el panadero tomó los mangos y le dio un pan dulce.
At the bakery, the baker took the mangoes and gave her a sweet bun.

a2-02.explain: Time words put events in order: primero (first), luego / después (then, afterwards), entonces (then, at that moment), al final (in the end). Ayer = yesterday; por la mañana / por la tarde = in the morning / in the afternoon. Watch out: de la mañana is only used after a clock time: a las seis de la mañana = at six in the morning.
examples: Por la mañana, su abuelo Ramón llegó con una caja azul.
In the morning, her grandfather Ramón came with a blue box.
Después, corrió por la calle Hidalgo con la llave en la mano.
After that, she ran along Hidalgo Street with the key in her hand.
Entonces, un perro pequeño salió y saltó a sus brazos.
Then a small dog came out and jumped into her arms.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.explain: Some key verbs have an irregular stem in the preterite and take no written accent: poner > pus- (puso), hacer > hic- (hice; he/she hizo, c becomes z), decir > dij- (dijo), tener > tuv- (tuve). On these stems the endings are -e for yo and -o for he/she: hice, tuve; puso, dijo. Ir and ser share fue: fue al supermercado (went), ¿Cuál fue el secreto? (was). Tuve que + infinitive = I had to. Watch out: hice, not 'hací' or 'hicé'.
examples: Luego fue al supermercado y compró carne, cebolla, tomates y papas.
Then he went to the supermarket and bought meat, onion, tomatoes and potatoes.
Después, puso aceite en la sartén y cocinó la carne.
After that, he put oil in the pan and cooked the meat.
Abuela, hice tu receta, pero el sabor no es igual.
Grandma, I made your recipe, but the taste isn't the same.

a2-03.explain: Both mean 'to be', but they aren't interchangeable. Estar: location and states or impressions right now: está rico (it tastes good), estoy en la puerta. Ser: identity, characteristics and comparisons such as no es igual (it isn't the same). Watch out: some adjectives change meaning. La comida está rica = the food tastes good; el señor es rico = the man is rich.
examples: Está rico, pero no es igual.
It's tasty, but it's not the same.
Porque estoy en la puerta de tu casa
Because I'm at the door of your house
¿Por qué no está en el cuaderno?
Why isn't it in the notebook?

a2-03.explain: Faltar and encantar work like gustar: the thing that is missing or that you love is the subject, so the verb agrees with it. The person goes in front as me, te, le, nos, les. Falta algo = something is missing; faltan dos ingredientes = two ingredients are missing. Me encanta = I love it (lit. it delights me); me encantan los tomates = I love tomatoes. Watch out: 'I love it' is me encanta, not 'yo encanto'.
examples: ¿Qué ingrediente falta, hijo?
What ingredient is missing, dear?
Solo falta un secreto.
Only one secret is missing.
¡Me encanta!
I love it!

a2-04.explain: The imperfect describes how things were and what used to happen: era, vivía, jugaba, tenía, tiraba. Endings: -aba for -ar verbs, -ía for -er/-ir verbs; ser is irregular (era). Siempre, todos los días and cuando era pequeño often signal it. Watch out: English 'played' can be one event or a habit; if 'used to' or 'would' fits, use the imperfect.
examples: Cuando Tomás era pequeño, vivía en un barrio de Medellín.
When Tomás was little, he lived in a neighborhood in Medellín.
Todos los días jugaba al fútbol en la calle con su hermana Natalia.
Every day he played soccer in the street with his sister Natalia.
Siempre tiraba el balón a la izquierda.
She always kicked the ball to the left.

a2-04.explain: The imperfect sets the scene: what was going on, the weather, how people felt. The preterite gives the event that happened within it: Faltaban dos minutos (background) cuando el árbitro pitó (event). Weather uses hacer: hacía sol = it was sunny. Watch out: English 'was + -ing' or 'was' describing a scene usually means imperfect; a single action ('he blew') means preterite.
examples: Faltaban dos minutos cuando el árbitro pitó un penalti.
Two minutes were left when the referee blew his whistle for a penalty.
Hacía mucho sol y el estadio estaba lleno de gente.
It was very sunny and the stadium was full of people.
Tomás estaba muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás was very nervous, but he remembered something.

a2-04.explain: Both mean 'to know'. Saber is for facts and information: sé adónde va a tirar = I know where she's going to kick (with an infinitive it means 'know how to': sé nadar). Conocer is for people, places and things you are familiar with, and takes a before a person: conocían a los dos hermanos. Both have irregular yo forms: sé, conozco. In the preterite, saber means 'found out': ¿Cómo lo supiste? Watch out: 'I know Natalia' is conozco a Natalia, not 'sé a Natalia'.
examples: Todos conocían a los dos hermanos.
Everybody knew the two siblings.
Yo sé adónde va a tirar
I know where she's going to kick
Conozco todos tus secretos.
I know all your secrets.

a2-05.explain: The imperfect paints the background before the action starts: time, weather, places, what existed. Era una tarde fría, llovía, vivía, había. Había means 'there was' and 'there were', and it stays singular: había un chico, había muchas cajas (not 'habían'). Watch out: weather and time in a description go in the imperfect (llovía, era de noche), not the preterite.
examples: Era una tarde fría de invierno en Santiago de Chile.
It was a cold winter afternoon in Santiago, Chile.
Llovía mucho y el viento golpeaba las ventanas.
It was raining a lot and the wind was beating against the windows.
Ella vivía en el número 7, y en la calle había un chico con una mochila roja.
She lived at number 7, and in the street there was a boy with a red backpack.

a2-05.explain: Form: estar + gerund (-ar > -ando, -er/-ir > -iendo; leer > leyendo). It describes an action in progress; with estaba, it was in progress at that past moment. A gerund can also show how someone did something: bajó corriendo = she hurried out (lit. got out running). Watch out: Spanish doesn't use this form for plans: 'I'm working tomorrow' = trabajo mañana.
examples: Valentina estaba en su sala, tomando té y mirando una serie.
Valentina was in her living room, drinking tea and watching a series.
Estaba trabajando y mi teléfono nuevo no tenía batería.
I was working and my new phone had no battery.
La mamá de Lisandro bajó corriendo con las llaves en la mano.
Lisandro's mother hurried out of the car with the keys in her hand.

a2-05.explain: The conditional makes requests and offers softer and more polite. Most verbs add -ía endings to the infinitive (gustaría); poder uses the short stem podr- (podría, podríamos). ¿Me podría ayudar? = Could you help me? (more polite than ¿Me puede ayudar?). ¿Te gustaría...? = Would you like...? (softer than ¿Quieres...?). Podríamos + infinitive = we could, for a suggestion. Watch out: write the accent on the í, and with gustaría the person goes in front: me, te, le gustaría.
examples: ¿Me podría ayudar?
Could you help me?
¿Te gustaría cenar con nosotros?
Would you like to have dinner with us?
Podríamos pedir unas empanadas.
We could order some empanadas.

a2-06.explain: The tú command is usually the he/she present form, stem change included: probar > prueba. Pronouns attach to the end of a positive command, and a written accent keeps the original stress: prueba + la = pruébala (try it); di + me + lo = dímelo (tell me). Watch out: don't split them ('prueba la') or put them first: la prueba means 'she tries it'.
examples: Si necesitas ayuda, dímelo.
If you need help, tell me.
Es para ti. Pruébala.
It's for you. Try it.
Ayúdame con las cajas.
Help me with the boxes.

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.explain: Por and para can both mean 'for', but they do different jobs. Para points to a goal or to the person who gets something: es para ti = it's for you; para tu primera casa = for your first home. Por is used for parts of the day (por la mañana, por la tarde) and for movement through or past a place: subir por la escalera = to go up the stairs; pasó por la puerta = he went past the door. Watch out: a gift for someone is para ti, not 'por ti' (por ti = because of you).
examples: Por la tarde, ella se sentó en el suelo y abrió la última caja.
In the afternoon, she sat down on the floor and opened the last box.
Mientras tanto, don Rafael pasó por la puerta abierta.
Meanwhile, don Rafael walked past the open door.
Es para ti.
It's for you.

a2-06.explain: The simple future says what will happen. Take the whole infinitive and add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án: estar > estaré (I will be), ser > seré, dar > dará (it will give). A pronoun goes before the verb: te dará = will give you. It is common in promises and predictions, like the grandmother's letter. For plans, everyday Spanish usually prefers ir a + infinitive: voy a comprar = I'm going to buy. Watch out: the accent is part of the ending: estaré, dará.
examples: Esta lámpara te dará luz y alegría, y yo siempre estaré contigo
This lamp will give you light and joy, and I will always be with you
Aquí seré feliz
I'll be happy here
Voy a comprar una ahora mismo en la tienda de la esquina
I'm going to buy one right now at the corner shop

a2-07.explain: Use the imperfect for routines and repeated actions (tocaba, llegaba, se sentaba), often with todas las tardes or siempre. Use the preterite for a single event that breaks the routine (empezó, se rompió, volvió), often with un jueves, de repente or diez minutos después. Watch out: English 'played' can be either; ask whether it was a habit or one occasion.
examples: Todas las tardes, Rodrigo tocaba la guitarra en una plaza de San Telmo, en Buenos Aires.
Every afternoon, Rodrigo played the guitar in a square in San Telmo, in Buenos Aires.
Un jueves, Rodrigo empezó una canción y de repente se rompió una cuerda.
One Thursday, Rodrigo started a song and suddenly a string broke.
Pero diez minutos después, la niña volvió con un señor de pelo blanco.
But ten minutes later, the girl came back with a white-haired man.

a2-07.explain: Indirect pronouns say to/for whom: me contó = told me; le cambió la cuerda = changed the string for him. When le or les comes before lo/la/los/las, it becomes se: se la mostró = showed it (la guitarra) to him; never 'le la'. Pronouns can attach to an infinitive, indirect first: pagártelo = to pay you for it.
examples: Ella me contó que tocas muy bien.
She told me you play very well.
Rodrigo se la mostró.
Rodrigo showed it to him.
Ernesto le cambió la cuerda en cinco minutos.
Ernesto changed the string for him in five minutes.
Quiero pagártelo.
I want to pay you for it.

a2-07.explain: Más + adjective + que = more ... than / -er than: más vieja que yo = older than me. After que, use subject pronouns (yo, tú), not mí or ti. Bueno has an irregular comparative, mejor (better); with a possessive or article it means 'best': su mejor alumna = his best student. Watch out: for quality say mejor, not 'más bueno'.
examples: Es muy bonita, pero es más vieja que yo.
It's very pretty, but it's older than I am.
Es más bonita que la radio.
It's prettier than the radio.
Julieta es su mejor alumna.
Julieta is his best student.

a2-08.explain: Nadie means 'nobody' and nada means 'nothing'. If the negative word comes after the verb, Spanish also puts no before the verb, and this double negative is correct: no vieron a nadie = they didn't see anybody; no veo nada = I can't see anything. If nadie comes first, you don't need no: Nadie respondió = Nobody answered. Watch out: use a before nadie when it is the person you see, call or help: no vieron a nadie.
examples: Cuando levantaron la cabeza, no vieron a nadie.
When they looked up, they didn't see anybody.
Nadie respondió.
Nobody answered.
No veo nada.
I can't see anything.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.explain: Three ways to say what is necessary, all followed by an infinitive. Hay que is general and never changes: hay que caminar despacio = you (everybody) have to walk slowly. Tener que is for a specific person, and tener changes: tenemos que hacer = we have to do. Deber means 'must' or 'should', often for advice: debes seguir el río = you must follow the river. Watch out: tener que needs que, but deber does not: debes seguir, not 'debes que seguir'.
examples: Si hay niebla, hay que caminar despacio.
If there is fog, you have to walk slowly.
Debes seguir el río
You must follow the river
¿Qué tenemos que hacer?
What do we have to do?

a2-08.explain: Ustedes is the plural 'you'. In Colombia and all of Latin America it is used for any group, friends or strangers; vosotros is only used in Spain. Ustedes takes the they-form of the verb: ustedes son = you are. The object pronoun for 'you all' is los (las for a group of women): los está buscando = he is looking for you; los busqué = I looked for you. Watch out: los can mean 'them' or 'you all'; the situation tells you which.
examples: Ustedes son los turistas
You're the tourists
Jairo los está buscando.
Jairo is looking for you.
Los busqué durante una hora.
I looked for you for an hour.

a2-09.explain: Form: he, has, ha, hemos, han + participle (-ar > -ado, -er/-ir > -ido); with usted it's ha: ¿ha trabajado? It links the past to now, especially life experience: nunca he llegado tarde = I've never been late. The participle never changes, and nothing goes between he and it. In Mexico and most of Latin America, for something that happened today people normally use the preterite: ¿Qué pasó? Watch out: 'I've been looking for 20 minutes' is llevo veinte minutos buscándola (present of llevar + gerund).
examples: Nunca he llegado tarde a una entrevista.
I've never been late for an interview.
¿Ha trabajado antes con clientes?
Have you worked with clients before? (usted)
He trabajado con tres tiendas pequeñas.
I have worked with three small shops.
Llevo veinte minutos buscándola.
I've been looking for it for twenty minutes.

a2-09.explain: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: me desperté, te despertaste, se despertó. Many daily-routine verbs are reflexive: despertarse (to wake up), vestirse (to get dressed; e > i: se vistió), sentarse (to sit down). Ponerse + adjective means 'to become': no se puso nerviosa = she didn't get nervous. Watch out: without se the verb needs an object and means doing it to someone else: despertó a su hermana = she woke her sister up; vistió al niño = she dressed the child.
examples: Daniela se despertó a las ocho y media, porque su alarma no sonó.
Daniela woke up at eight thirty because her alarm didn't go off.
Se vistió rápidamente, tomó su currículum y salió corriendo de casa.
She got dressed quickly, grabbed her résumé and ran out of the house.
La señora mayor entró en la sala y se sentó junto a la jefa.
The older woman came into the room and sat down next to the boss.

a2-09.explain: Tú is informal; usted is formal and uses the he/she verb form: (usted) llega tarde = you're late, but (tú) llegas tarde. The interviewer, Mrs. Ortega, uses usted with Daniela the whole time (llega, tiene, ¿ha trabajado?, el puesto es suyo); Daniela is polite to the older woman too (la acompaño). The older woman and the man at the metro use tú (¿sabes?, no te vi), and so does the founder later (tú me ayudaste). Watch out: llega, tiene or suyo can mean 'he/she/his/her' or 'you/yours (usted)'; context decides.
examples: —Llega tarde —dijo—, y tiene la camisa manchada.
"You're late," she said, "and your shirt is stained."
Hija, ¿sabes dónde está la oficina de diseño?
Dear, do you know where the design office is?
Perdona, no te vi.
Sorry, I didn't see you.
El puesto es suyo.
The position is yours. (usted)

a2-10.explain: Más + adjective + que compares two things: más bonito que antes = prettier than before. The superlative is el/la + noun + más + adjective + de: el farol más grande de la historia = the biggest lantern in history. Watch out: English says 'in', Spanish says de: la fiesta más importante del pueblo = the most important festival in the village.
examples: Era más bonito que antes.
It was prettier than before.
Es el farol más grande de la historia del pueblo.
It's the biggest lantern in the history of the village.
Hiciste una familia más grande.
You made a bigger family.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
a2-10.explain: Present perfect: he/has/ha + participle, for experience up to now: nunca he visto = I have never seen. Past perfect: había + participle, for something that happened before another past moment: había aprendido = she had learned. The participle never changes. Watch out: some participles are irregular: visto (ver), hecho (hacer), dicho (decir), puesto (poner).
examples: Nunca he visto trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
I've never seen this village work so fast.
Había aprendido que un pueblo unido puede hacer cosas increíbles.
She had learned that a united village can do incredible things.
El agua había mojado el papel y una pata del toro estaba en el suelo.
The water had soaked the paper and one of the bull's legs was on the floor.

a2-10.explain: Demonstratives point to things and times. Este/esta = this: near the speaker, or now (este pueblo, esta vez). Ese/esa = that: a bit further away, or a time already mentioned (ese año). Aquel/aquella = that: far away, often a moment in the distant past (aquella noche). They agree with the noun: este pueblo, esta vez, aquel día, aquella noche. Watch out: esta (this) has no accent; está (is) does.
examples: Ese año tenía una misión especial.
That year she had a special mission.
Aunque llovió la noche anterior, aquella fue la mejor noche de su vida.
Although it rained the night before, that was the best night of her life.
Y esta vez no lloró de tristeza.
And this time she didn't cry from sadness.
